Anne: heads-up deploy-bot preflight failed on release/2026-03-22 — IAM module plan shows provider version drift, plan would recreate service-account roles. Holding apply until we decide. /cc @lisa-pm

deploy-bot: PRE-FLIGHT: terraform plan failed. Modules affected: iam (module.accounts). Diff: recreates 2 google_service_account, modifies 1 google_project_iam_binding. Error: provider.google v4.3.0 vs pinned v4.2.1. Suggests pin or upgrade. Full output:
```
Error: Incompatible provider version
  on modules/iam/main.tf line 12, in resource "google_service_account":
  provider "google" does not meet required version
```

Sam: can we pin provider to 4.2.1 in release branch and run partial apply for non-iam modules? prefer not to block network/netpol changes.

Marta: agree, but IAM change is in release notes (security) — PM needs to sign off. @lisa-pm do you want us to pause the whole cutover?

Lisa-pm: pause for now. don't ship IAM role changes without security review. update release notes to note rollback path, ETA to unblock?

Ryan-oncall: +1 to pause. also tag sec-oncall. If we need a quick unblock: option A) pin provider and apply everything except module. Option B) create canary for tenant-x only.

Kai: If we pin provider, ensure we add a provider constraint in versions.tf and run `terraform providers lock` then `git push`. Sample:
```
# versions.tf
terraform {
  required_providers {
    google = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google"
      version = "~> 4.2.1"
    }
  }
}
```
Then `terraform init -upgrade=false` and `terraform plan`.

Sam: I'll prepare the pin PR and a selective apply plan: `terraform apply -target=module.network -target=module.ipam -var 'release=2026-03-22'`

Marta: add an explicit rollback note: how to revert IAM if we land by mistake. Put steps in release notes and in the deploybot runbook.
